q.text: So, what is it you do around here?
How would you describe your work to a new migrant?
Tell our readers what you do in {fort}.
What's your trade?
What does the job of {prof} actually involve?
What does a soldier do all day when nothing is attacking?
What do you do all day?
What do you do around here?

trade_low.text: I'm {a_prof}, and I'm still learning. The first hundred mistakes are behind me. The next hundred are scheduled.
I'm {a_prof}. Not a good one yet, but nobody has been hurt, which is more than some trades can say.
{a_prof_cap}, technically. The records rate me '{trade_level}', which I am choosing to read as a compliment.
I'm {a_prof}, and I'm getting better every week. Ask me again next year.
I'm {a_prof}. I'm not good at it yet, and everybody watching me work makes sure I know it.

trade_mid.text: I'm {a_prof}. A {trade_level} one, by the records, which means I'm trusted with the job but not yet with the speech about it.
I'm the fort's {prof}. I know the work well enough now that I only swear at it out of habit.
{a_prof_cap}. It's honest work. I'd call myself {trade_level} at it, and so would the records, so there.
I'm {a_prof}, and I'm good at it. Not legendary, but the work gets done and it gets done right.
I'm {a_prof}. Competent enough that they keep giving me more of it.
I'm {a_prof}. Good enough to be trusted, still learning enough to be careful.
{a_prof_cap}. The records say {trade_level}. My friends say 'fine'. I'll take either.

trade_high.text: I'm {a_trade_title}. I don't say it to boast. I say it because it's carved on my door.
I'm {a_prof}. {a_trade_title_cap}, if you want the full title, and the fort does tend to want it.
I'm {a_prof}, and I'm very good at it. When something goes wrong in my line of work, they come and fetch me.
I'm {a_trade_title}. Years of practice. I still enjoy it, which surprises everyone, including me.
I'm {a_trade_title}, so naturally they ask me to haul stone.
I'm {a_prof}, and I've been at it long enough to be called {a_trade_title}. My hands know the work better than my head does.
{a_trade_title_cap}. The young ones come and watch me work. I pretend not to notice.
I'm {a_prof}. Years of it. There isn't much in my trade that can surprise me now.

drills.text: They list me as {a_prof}, but these days I spend more time in the barracks with {squad} than at my old trade.
On paper I'm {a_prof}. In practice I'm in {squad}, and most of my days go to drilling.
I used to be {a_prof}. Then I joined {squad}, and now my best skill is {milskill}.
I'm {a_prof} by trade and a soldier by roster. Honestly, I've come to like the drills.
I'm {a_prof}, supposedly. I haven't touched my trade in so long I'd need a refresher.
I'm {a_prof}, officially. Unofficially, I'm whoever {squad} needs me to be this week.
My trade is {prof}, but the barracks have had more of me than the workshop lately. I'm best at {milskill} now.
{a_prof_cap} by trade. These days the sergeant knows my face better than my old foreman does.

soldier.text: I'm a soldier in {squad}. We train, we eat, we train again. I'm best at {milskill}.
I'm with {squad}. My job is to be ready, which mostly means practising {milskill} until it's boring.
Train, mostly, with {squad}. Somebody has to stand between {fort} and whatever comes up from below.
Drills with {squad}, then supper. It's a good life when nothing is attacking, and a short one when something is.
I'm in {squad}. I train until my arms ache, then they ask me to train some more.
I'm in {squad}. We drill until we can do it asleep, and then we drill some more.
Soldiering. I'm with {squad}, and my best skill is {milskill}. I'd rather not have to prove it.
I serve in {squad}. Most days are training. Some days, I hope, will stay that way.

office.text: I'm the {prof}. It means meetings, complaints and a chair that is slightly better than everyone else's.
Being {prof} is mostly listening. Everybody in {fort} has an opinion, and they bring every one of them to me.
I'm the {prof}. People think it's an easy post. People are welcome to try it.
I'm the {prof}, and I enjoy it. Somebody has to keep this place organised, and I happen to like lists.
I'm the {prof}, and the job never ends. I'd swap it for a pick most days.
I'm the {prof}. If something goes wrong in {fort}, it ends up on my desk, usually with a complaint attached.

plain.text: I'm {a_prof}. I do what the work orders say, and the work orders say a lot.
{a_prof_cap}, by trade. These days I take whatever job is closest, like most of {fort}.
I'm {a_prof}. It isn't glamorous, but the fort wouldn't run without it, and I remind them of that often.
I'm {a_prof}, and I like it fine. Good work, decent company, and the ale is close.
I'm {a_prof}. Some days I wonder if anybody notices.

child.text: I play. And I watch the grown-ups work, so I know how to do it better when I'm big.
I'm a child. I mostly run about. The soldiers let me watch them drill if I'm quiet.
Playing, mostly. When I grow up I'm going to be the best miner in {fort}.
I help. Sometimes. Mostly I'm told to stop helping.

baby.text: (The subject fell asleep mid-question. We have had worse interviews.)

drills.text: FROM THE WORKSHOP TO THE BARRACKS

q.text: With {soldiers} of our {pop} dwarves on the militia rolls, do you ever get called up for drills?
Are you in the militia?
Do you ever train with the soldiers?

in_squad.text: Called up? I'm in {squad}. I spend more time in the barracks than in my own bed.
I'm in {squad}, so yes, every week. My {milskill} has never been better.
I'm in {squad}. The drills are long, but you learn who you can rely on.
I'm in {squad}, and I enjoy it. A good day's training and a mug afterwards. What else is there?
I'm in {squad}. My feet hurt, my arms hurt, and the sergeant is never satisfied.

civilian_few.text: Somebody has to keep the fort running while the rest of them drill. That somebody is me.
I'm one of the few left off the rolls. I keep very quiet in case anybody notices.
Not yet. With {soldiers} of us in squads already, I think the fort can spare one {prof}.
I'm not in a squad, and I'm grateful to everyone who is.

civilian.text: Not me. I'm happy to let the {soldiers} who signed up do the fighting.
I'm not in a squad. I respect the ones who are. From a distance.
I've thought about it. Then I watch them drill in the rain and I stop thinking about it.
No, but I cheer them on. Every fort needs an audience.

q.text: How are you feeling these days?
How is life in {fort} treating you?
How are your spirits this {season}?
Are you happy here?
Our readers worry about you. How are you holding up?

ecstatic.text: Never better. I wake up smiling and I can't explain it. Possibly the ale.
Wonderful. Honestly wonderful. I keep waiting for something to go wrong and it doesn't.
I've never been happier. Write that down before something changes it.
Marvellous. I hummed all the way down the stairs this morning, and I don't hum.
Couldn't be better. Whatever this fort is doing, it should keep doing it.
On top of the mountain, and I live under it. Make of that what you will.
Happier than I have any right to be. I'm not asking questions.

happy.text: Good, thank you. I've got work, friends and a full mug. That's the whole list.
Happy, mostly. Life in {fort} suits me.
Very well. I sleep well, I eat well, and nobody has thrown anything at me this week.
Pretty good. The work is steady and the company is decent.
Well, thank you. Every day has something good in it, if you look.
Cheerful. Somebody told me I was whistling yesterday. I deny it.
Good. Not perfect, but good. I'll take good.

content.text: Fine. Not dancing, not crying. Steady.
Content, I'd say. Some good days, some long ones.
I'm all right. Ask me again after supper.
Middling. Which, down here, counts as a win.
Getting by. No complaints worth printing.

stressed.text: Tired. Things are piling up and I'm not sure who is going to clear them.
Not great, if I'm honest. Nothing terrible, just one thing after another.
I've been better. I'm trying to keep my temper, which takes effort.

very_stressed.text: Badly. I'm one bad meal away from shouting at somebody.
Poorly. I keep my head down and hope the week ends soon.
Please don't print this, but I'm close to the edge.

breaking.text: I'd rather not talk about it. Leave me alone. Please.
I'm not well. I don't want to talk. I want somebody to fix things.
Ask me something else. Anything else.

ecstatic.text: HUMMING ALL THE WAY DOWN THE STAIRS
HAPPIER THAN THEY HAVE ANY RIGHT TO BE

happy.text: 'EVERY DAY HAS SOMETHING GOOD IN IT'

very_stressed.text: ONE BAD MEAL FROM THE EDGE

q.text: What's been the best part of your week?
Anything cheered you up lately?
What was the last thing that put a smile on your face?
We hear you've been catching the performances. Any good?
We hear you've been performing. How did it go?
We hear you've been learning something new?
You've been teaching, we're told. How are the students?

show.text: I watched a performance the other night and I'm still thinking about it. Good stuff.
The performances. I caught a show and forgot about work for a whole evening.
I went to see the performers. Somebody sang about a carp and the whole room cried.
A performance. The poet was good. The dancer was better. I clapped until my hands hurt.

perform.text: I performed! People listened. Some of them even stayed to the end.
I got up and performed for a crowd. My knees shook, but my voice didn't.
Performing for the fort. There's nothing like a room that goes quiet for you.
I performed for the fort. Nobody threw anything, which I'm told is a good review.

drunk.text: I had a few drinks and felt wonderful. I recommend it. In moderation. Or not.
A very good night at the tavern. I don't remember all of it, which is how I know it was good.
Drinking, honestly. Last night I was the happiest dwarf in {fort}, for about an hour.
A night at the tavern. Good drink, loud company, a song I won't repeat in print.

skill.text: I'm getting better at my work. You can feel it in your hands when something finally clicks.
I learned something new. Small thing, but I've been waiting years to get it right.
Improving. Every day a little better. It adds up.
I finally got the hang of something I'd been struggling with. Small victory. Big grin.

teach.text: Teaching. Watching somebody finally get it is better than getting it yourself.
I've been passing on what I know. The young ones listen more than they let on.
I had a student get something right on the first try. I was prouder than they were.

talk.text: A good long talk with a friend. We solved most of the fort's problems, in theory.
Conversation. I sat with a few dwarves and talked until the lamps burned down.
Somebody listened to me properly for once. That's rarer than gold down here.
A long chat over supper. We disagreed about everything and enjoyed every minute.

friend.text: I made a new friend. At my age! It turns out we hate the same things.
Making a friend. We met over a mug and now we sit together at meals.
A new friend. You don't expect it this deep under the mountain, but there you go.

work.text: A good day's work. I finished what I started and nobody needed it redone.
Work, believe it or not. Some days the job just goes right.
I had a day where everything I touched came out well. I'll be talking about it for weeks.

bedroom.text: My bedroom. I love that room. Four walls, a bed and a door that shuts.
Going to bed, honestly. I've got a fine room and I enjoy every minute in it.
My room. Whoever dug it knew what they were doing.

meal.text: A really good meal. I could taste every ingredient, and most of them were on purpose.
Supper the other night. The cook outdid themselves.
Food. A proper hot meal. It fixes most things.

building.text: I stopped to admire some of the stonework. Somebody in this fort has real talent.
The buildings. I walked past a well-made room and just stood there for a while.
Admiring the halls. A fort that looks this good is a fort worth living in.

temple.text: A ceremony at the temple. I came out feeling lighter than I went in.
Prayer, and the rites. It's good to stop and remember there's more than work.
The temple. I joined the rites and felt, for once, that somebody was listening.
The rites at the temple. Quiet, candles, and a feeling I can't quite name.

book.text: Reading. I found a book I hadn't read and lost a whole afternoon in it.
Study. I've been reading and thinking, and I think I understand a little more than before.
A good book. Don't laugh. Some of us read.

spar.text: Sparring. I held my own against a dwarf twice my size.
A good sparring match. Nothing broken, everything learned.
Practice fights. I won one. I'm not saying which one.

clothes.text: I've got clothes I actually like. Small thing, but it makes the day better.
New clothes. Well made. I wear them everywhere.
Something nice to wear. You feel different in good cloth.

play.text: Playing! I had a toy and a whole afternoon.
Make-believe. I was a forgotten beast and everybody ran away.
Games. I won some and I lost some and then I made up new rules.

family.text: My family has grown. I still can't quite believe it.
Family news. The best kind. I'm smiling just thinking about it.
A new member of the family. Everything else this week is small next to that.

argue.text: I won an argument. Fair and square. I was right and now everybody knows it.
A lively debate. I enjoyed every minute and so did the other dwarf, eventually.
A good argument. Nothing clears the head like being right out loud.

help.text: I helped somebody who needed it. That's a good feeling.
I looked after a dwarf who couldn't look after themselves for a bit. Glad I could.
Lending a hand. It's nice to be useful outside the work orders.

other.text: Small things. A quiet moment, a good mug. That's enough for me.
Hard to say. A few good days in a row, and nothing went wrong.
Nothing grand. I'm just having a decent week.

perform.text: THE CROWD WENT QUIET FOR THIS PERFORMER

drunk.text: A VERY GOOD NIGHT AT THE TAVERN

skill.text: A SMALL VICTORY, A BIG GRIN

bedroom.text: FOUR WALLS AND A DOOR THAT SHUTS

meal.text: IN PRAISE OF A HOT MEAL

building.text: STOPPED IN THEIR TRACKS BY STONEWORK

q.text: Anything bothering you lately?
Any complaints for the overseer?
What's the worst thing that happened to you this week?
How are you finding the weather?
We hear there's been a smell. Have you noticed?

rain.text: The rain. I went outside for one minute and came back soaked to the beard.
Getting rained on. Dwarves were not made to have water fall on them from above.
The weather. I don't mind water in a mug. I mind it down my collar.

miasma.text: The smell. Something is rotting somewhere and the whole corridor knows it.
Miasma. Somebody needs to clear whatever is lying about before it walks off by itself.
The stink. I won't say where. You'll find it yourself.

argue.text: An argument. Somebody said something and I said something back and now it's a whole thing.
A quarrel with another dwarf. I'm right, of course, but it still spoils the week.
I fell out with somebody. We'll make up. Eventually. Possibly.

crowded.text: The dining hall is packed. I had to eat standing up with somebody's elbow in my soup.
Crowded tables. More chairs, please. Or fewer dwarves at supper.
Meals are a scrum. I'd like to sit down for one, just once.

mud.text: I had to sleep in the mud. Not a bed, not a floor. Mud.
Sleeping rough. My back hasn't forgiven me.
Bedtime on the ground. I'm not a dog. Well, the dogs get beds.

nobed.text: I don't have a bedroom. I'd settle for a cupboard with a door.
No room of my own. I sleep wherever I fall, and I fall in some odd places.
A bedroom, or the lack of one. Is that too much to ask?

bored_show.text: I went to a performance and it bored me stiff. I've seen better arguments in the dining hall.
A performance that went on forever. I counted the ceiling tiles twice.
Bad theatre. Somebody recited for an hour and I'll never get it back.

death.text: Seeing the dead. You don't forget a thing like that.
Death. It's been close this week, and it shakes you.
A body. I'd rather not say more.

hurt.text: I got hurt. Not badly. Badly enough to complain about, though.
Pain. I took a knock and I'm still feeling it.
An injury. The doctor says it'll heal. The doctor says that about everything.

hunger.text: I've been hungry. Properly hungry, the kind that makes you mean.
Food, or the lack of it, when I wanted it.
My stomach. It's been empty too often.

thirst.text: I've been thirsty, and not the good kind. I want a drink and I want it now.
No drink when I needed one. Unacceptable.
Thirst. A dwarf without a drink is a dwarf without patience.

other.text: Nothing I want printed. Let's say the week could have gone better.
One of those weeks. You know the kind.

nobed.text: A CUPBOARD WITH A DOOR, PLEASE

q.text: Is there anything you've been missing lately?
If the overseer granted you one wish, what would it be?
What would make your week?

acquire.text: Something new to call my own. A ring, a figurine, anything. I just want to own a nice thing.
Shopping. I'd love to pick up something pretty when the next caravan comes.
Possessions. Everyone else seems to have nicer things than me.
Something nice of my own. A bracelet, a cup with a bit of gold on it. I'm not fussy. I'm a little fussy.
A trinket. Everyone deserves one good thing that's theirs and nobody else's.

craft.text: Making something with my own hands. Not for an order. Just for me.
Crafting. I miss sitting down and making something from scratch.
A free hour at a workbench. I've got an idea and nowhere to make it.
To make something. I've had a figurine in my head for a month and nowhere to carve it.
Time at a bench with no work order attached. Just me and an idea.

friends.text: Time with my friends. We all work different shifts and never see each other.
My friends. I'd give a week's ale for one evening with them.
Company. Good company, not just whoever is at the next table.
An evening with my friends. Just one. We keep missing each other.

extravagant.text: Something a bit grand. Fine clothes, a fancy room. Life is too short for plain stone.
Luxury. Gold trim, gems on the door, the works. Is that so wrong?
A little extravagance. I'm tired of making do.
Fine things. A carved chair, a coloured cloak. Something nobody needs and everybody admires.

meal.text: A really good meal. Something cooked properly, not just whatever is nearest.
Proper food. A lavish meal I can sit down to and take my time over.
Fine dining. I'd settle for a good roast eaten slowly.

fight.text: A good fight. Nothing serious. Just something to test myself against.
Fighting. I've got energy and nowhere to put it.
A scrap. I'm not looking for trouble, but I wouldn't run from it.

excitement.text: Excitement. Anything. Even a small cave-in would liven things up. A small one.
Something to happen. Every day here is the same.
A thrill. I'm bored stiff and the walls are starting to look interesting.

wander.text: A walk. A long one, with nowhere to be at the end of it.
Wandering. I want to see a bit of the world outside these halls.
Room to roam. I've walked every corridor in {fort} twice.

help.text: To be useful to somebody. Not a work order, a real person who needs a hand.
Helping out. I like knowing I made somebody's day easier.
A chance to lend a hand. It's been too long.

rest.text: A day off. One. I'd spend it doing absolutely nothing.
Rest. I want to sit down and not be asked to get up.
Taking it easy. I've forgotten how.

merry.text: A party. Music, drink, dancing, the lot.
Merriment. The fort could do with a celebration.
A good night out at the tavern with everyone there.

train.text: Proper weapons practice. I'm getting rusty.
Training. A soldier who doesn't drill is just a dwarf with a sword.
Time in the barracks. I'd like to keep my edge.

creative.text: Room to be creative. Write something, carve something, sing something.
Making something new. Something nobody has asked for.
A creative afternoon. I've got ideas piling up.

art.text: Something beautiful to look at. A good engraving, a fine statue.
Art. I'd walk a long way to see something well made.
Admiring something lovely. The fort could use a few more pretty things.

romance.text: Romance. There, I said it. Print it in small type.
Somebody special. I'm not getting any younger.
Love, if you must know. The fort is big. Somebody must be out there.

busy.text: Something to do. Idle hands, and all that.
Work. Real work. I'm going spare with nothing to do.
A job. Any job. I'll even haul.

practice.text: Time to practise my craft. I'm slipping.
Practice. A skill you don't use goes stale.
Time at my trade. I miss the work.

trouble.text: A bit of mischief. Nothing serious. Probably.
Trouble. Just a little. To keep things interesting.
Stirring something up. It's been too quiet.

think.text: Something to think about. A real puzzle, not a work order.
Deep thought. A quiet room and a hard question.
Ideas. I'd like to ponder something properly.

eloquence.text: To hear somebody speak well. A good speech, a good poem.
Eloquence. Most talk down here is about rocks.
Somebody who can turn a phrase. I'd sit and listen all night.

self.text: A quiet moment to think about my life. Where it's going.
Time to reflect. I've been too busy to ask myself how I'm doing.
Some peace to sort out my own head.

tradition.text: A bit of tradition. Things done properly, the old way.
The old customs. Everyone rushes these days.
Respect for how things were done in the mountainhomes.

learn.text: To learn something new. Anything. I'm hungry for it.
Lessons. A book, a teacher, a new skill.
Knowledge. I want to know how things work.

family.text: Time with my family. We pass each other in the halls and that's it.
My family. I'd like a quiet meal with them.
Family time. Work keeps getting in the way.

drink.text: A drink. A proper one, in a mug, sitting down.
Booze. It's been too long since I had a really good one.

animal.text: To see some animals. Something with fur that doesn't want anything from me.
Animals. I'd like to spend time in the pasture.
A pet to scratch behind the ears.

acquire.text: IN NEED OF A NICE THING
ONE GOOD THING OF THEIR OWN

friends.text: A WEEK'S ALE FOR AN EVENING WITH FRIENDS

fight.text: ENERGY AND NOWHERE TO PUT IT

wander.text: THE CALL OF THE OPEN ROAD

busy.text: GOING SPARE WITH NOTHING TO DO

q.text: Do you follow a god?
Who do you pray to?
Does faith play a part in your life down here?
Have you had time to pray lately?

deity.text: I pray to {deity}. Not every day, but when it counts.
{deity}. My family has always prayed there, and so do I.
{deity} watches over me. I try to give them a quiet word now and then.
{deity}, and I think they're listening. Things have gone well lately.
{deity}. Though I'd like a word with them about this week.

many.text: {deity}, mostly, and {deity2} when that doesn't work.
I keep {deity} and {deity2} in my prayers. It's good to have options.
{deity} and {deity2}. I try not to play favourites.

pray_need.text: Not enough. I owe {deity} a prayer, and I can feel it.
No, and it's weighing on me. I need to find a quiet hour with {deity}.
Barely. {deity} must think I've forgotten them. I haven't. I've been busy.

none.text: Not really. I believe in good stone and a full mug.
I keep my own counsel. The gods have enough dwarves to worry about.
No god for me. I trust what I can hold.

deity.text: A QUIET WORD WITH THE GODS

q.text: Tell us about your family.
Any news of the children?
Is there anyone special in your life?
Any family here in {fort}?

spouse.text: I'm married to {kin}. Best decision I ever made, and I tell them so twice a year.
{kin} and I are married. We argue about everything and agree about everything that matters.
My spouse, {kin}. They put up with me, which is more than most would.
{kin}. We're married, and I'd do it again tomorrow.
{kin} and I are married. We don't see enough of each other with all this work.
{kin}. We've been married a while now. Still my favourite dwarf in {fort}.

lover.text: There's {kin}. We're not married. Yet. Don't print that. Oh, you're printing it.
{kin}, if you must know. We're courting. Slowly. Dwarvishly.
I've been seeing {kin}. It's early days, but it's good.

widowed.text: I was married to {kin}. They're gone now. I still set out two mugs some nights.
My spouse, {kin}, is no longer with us. I don't talk about it much.
{kin}. We had good years. I think about them every day.

children.text: I have {kids}. {child} is the one who keeps me up at night, in every sense.
{kids_cap}, and {child} takes after me, poor thing.
My children. {child} especially. I'm prouder than I let on.

parents.text: My parents, {kin} and {kin2}. They still tell me how to do my job.
{kin} and {kin2}. My parents. They're well, and they have opinions.
I've got my mother and father, {kin} and {kin2}. Every family dinner is a debate.

parent.text: {kin}. My {rel}. Still telling me to stand up straight.
My {rel}, {kin}. We're close. Closer than most.
{kin}, my {rel}. Wise, stubborn, usually right. I hate that.

orphan.text: My parents have passed on. I carry them with me.
No family left, not living. The fort is my family now.
My people are gone. I don't dwell on it, but I don't forget.

none.text: Nobody in particular. My friends, I suppose. And whoever sits next to me at supper.
No family here. The fort is family enough, most days.
Not yet. I'm keeping an eye out. A dwarf can hope.
No one special, and I'm fine with that. More ale for me.
Nobody. Some nights that's harder than others.
Just me. The fort keeps me busy enough.
Nobody yet. I'm told there's a dwarf for everyone. I'm told a lot of things.
Not family, but good friends. That's plenty.

baby.text: (The subject pointed at {kin}, its {rel}, and then at the ceiling.)
(The subject said something that sounded like '{kin}'. It may have been a burp.)

parents.text: STILL TOLD HOW TO DO THE JOB

q.text: What do you make of {fort} these days?
How is the fort doing, from where you stand?
Our count says the cellars hold {drinks} drinks. Enough?
The drink is running low. How is the fort coping?
Food is short this season. How are you managing?
Our count is {thread} spools of thread in storage. Any idea what it's for?
{fort} is up to {pop} dwarves. Too crowded?
{fort} is only {fort_days} days old. How is the new place?
There are {herd} animals in the herds now. Do you ever visit them?
The caverns are open below us. Do you ever go down?

drinks_high.text: {drinks} drinks? That's the best number I've heard all year. We'll manage.
Plenty to drink. A fort with full cellars is a fort that gets things done.
The cellars are full and the mood is good. Coincidence? No.

drinks_low.text: Badly. A dwarf can go without many things. Drink is not one of them.
Everyone's watching the barrels. Somebody needs to get the still going.
Short tempers, short drinks. Fix it, please.

food_low.text: We tighten our belts and eat what's there. Somebody plant something, quickly.
Hungry, mostly. The farmers are doing what they can.
Not well. You notice how much you think about food when there isn't any.

food_high.text: Well fed, thank you. Nobody is going hungry here.
The stores are full. I've had a hot meal every day this week.
We eat well in {fort}. Better than most forts, I'd wager.

thread_glut.text: {thread} spools? I have no idea. I think somebody likes spinning.
Thread? I couldn't tell you. We could wrap the whole mountain twice.
Clothes for everybody, I hope. Then clothes for everybody again.

pop_big.text: It's busy. {pop} dwarves means a queue for everything, but there's always somebody to talk to.
Crowded, but lively. I like a full dining hall.
There are faces I don't recognise any more. That's how you know a fort has made it.

young_fort.text: Still finding my way around. Half the corridors aren't dug yet.
It's new, it's rough, and it's ours. Give it a year.
Everything is unfinished, including me. We'll get there.

old_fort.text: {fort} has been here a while now. It feels like home.
It's settled. The halls are worn smooth and everyone knows their place.
Old enough to have stories, young enough to make more.

herd_big.text: I visit sometimes. {herd} animals means there's always something chewing.
The pastures are full. I like the animals. They don't ask for work orders.
I go down to the pasture when I need a quiet minute. The animals don't judge.

caverns.text: Down there? Only if I'm made to. Things live in the dark that don't want visitors.
I've been down once. The mushrooms are taller than the trees outside. I came back up.
Never. The caverns can keep themselves to themselves.

plain.text: {fort} is doing all right. Could be worse. Has been worse.
It's a decent fort. Good stone, good dwarves, mostly.
I like it here. Don't tell the overseer, they'll get ideas.

thread_glut.text: ENOUGH THREAD TO WRAP THE MOUNTAIN

pop_big.text: {pop} DWARVES AND A QUEUE FOR EVERYTHING

herd_big.text: A QUIET MINUTE IN THE PASTURE

caverns.text: THE CAVERNS CAN KEEP TO THEMSELVES

q.text: How has the fort been since {lastdead} died?
{moody} has locked themselves in a workshop. Any idea what they're making?
Have you seen {artifact_new} yet?
A new wave of migrants has arrived. Any advice for them?
There's a new baby in the fort. Have you seen it?
There was a wedding this week. Were you there?
The merchants are at the depot. Buying anything?
Word is we finally have contact with {contact_civ}. What do you make of it?
Have you heard? {envoy_back} came back from {contact_site} with a deal.
{contact_civ} know we exist now. Good thing?
{envoy} rode out for {envoy_site}. Will it work?
We've sent {envoy} to talk trade with {envoy_civ}. Your thoughts?
What would you want {envoy_civ} to bring us, if {envoy} talks them into it?

death_week.text: Quieter. You notice the empty seat at supper. {lastdead} was one of us.
I knew {lastdead} a little. Everybody did. The fort feels smaller now.
We'll carve {lastdead} a good slab. It's the least we can do.
Sad. We carry on, because that's what dwarves do, but it's sad.

mood_open.text: No idea. Nobody goes near the door. Whatever it is, I hope it's worth the wait.
Something extraordinary, or something terrible. With a mood you never know.
I left a mug outside the door. It was gone in the morning. That's all I know.
I walk the long way round so I don't disturb them. Whatever it is, the fort will be talking about it for years.
I hope they get what they need. A mood that goes wrong is a terrible thing.

mood_done.text: I saw it. {artifact_new}. I don't know what I expected, but it wasn't that, and it was better.
Yes. {artifact_maker} made something the whole fort will talk about for years.
I queued to see it. Worth the queue.

artifact_week.text: I've seen {artifact_new}. A real artifact, here in {fort}. We're on the map now.
Yes. You stand there and you just look at it. Hard to believe a dwarf made it.
Only from the back of the crowd. Everyone wanted a look.

migrants_week.text: Find a bed before somebody else does. Then find the tavern.
Keep your head down, learn the corridors, and never volunteer to haul.
Learn where the dining hall is first. Everything else can wait.

birth_week.text: I have. Small, loud and already bearded. A proper dwarf.
Yes. The parents look exhausted and delighted, which is about right.
Not yet. I can hear it, though. The whole corridor can hear it.

marriage_week.text: I was. Good speeches, better ale. I cried, but only a little.
I heard it from the dining hall. It sounded like a fine party.
No, but I sent my best. Somebody has to keep working.

caravan_here.text: I'm going to look. I never buy anything. I like looking.
If they've got good cloth, maybe. If it's elf wood, absolutely not.
The broker does the buying. I just watch the haggling. Best show in the fort.

contact_new.text: Good. More caravans, more things to buy, more strangers to stare at in the tavern.
It means a caravan, eventually. I've been saving a mug for something foreign to drink.
I hope {contact_civ} like stone. We have a great deal of stone.
Everybody's talking about it. {envoy_back} has told the story four times tonight and it got better every time.
Contact is fine. Contact is how wars start too. Let's see what they bring first.

envoys_out.text: If anyone can talk {envoy_civ} into trading, it's {envoy}. That dwarf could sell gravel to a quarry.
Cloth. Spices. Anything that isn't another rock. I'd settle for a new kind of cheese.
I hope {envoy} packed enough to drink. {envoy_site} is a long walk.
It's a long way to {envoy_site} with nothing but a letter. Braver than me.
We'll know by the next season. Either a caravan turns up or {envoy} does, looking sheepish.

mood_done.text: THE ARTIFACT EVERYONE IS TALKING ABOUT

caravan_here.text: THE BEST SHOW IN THE FORT: HAGGLING

q.text: Did you hear what happened to {past_fort}?
Is it true that {record_fort} once had {record}?
{fort} holds a record: {record}. Proud?

past_fort.text: I heard. {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. It's a hard world out there.
Everybody's heard. {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. We try to learn from it.
Only what the travellers say: {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. I hope we do better here.

record_past.text: So they say. I wasn't there, and from the sound of it, I'm glad.
That's the story. I hope nobody here gets ideas.
I've heard that one. Every fort needs a legend. That was theirs.

record_here.text: Proud? Confused, mostly. But yes, a little proud.
Somebody has to hold the record. Might as well be us.
I didn't know it was a competition. Apparently we're winning.

q.text: We're at war with {enemy}. Any message for them?
How do you feel about the war with {enemy}?

goblin.text: Come and try it. We have walls, we have soldiers, and we have very long memories.
Goblins. I'd tell them to go home, but I'm not sure they have one.
Stay away from {fort}. We drill every day for exactly this.

elven.text: Elves. They're at war with us over trees, I expect. It's always trees.
Tell them we're sorry about the logs. We're not sorry about the logs.
Let them come. We'll offer them a nice wooden chair.

human.text: Humans. Big, slow, and a long way off. I'll worry when I see them.
Tell them we're happy to trade instead, if they'll stop being silly.
I've no quarrel with them personally. But if they come, they'll find us ready.

other.text: Stay where you are and we'll stay where we are. That's my message.
We're ready for them. That's all I'll say.

goblin.text: A MESSAGE FOR {enemy}: 'COME AND TRY IT'

q.text: Any last words for our readers?
Anything else you'd like to say?
Before we go to print, anything to add?
Any parting words?

any.text: Drink plenty, sleep when you can, and never stand under anything the miners are working on.
Look after each other. The mountain won't do it for you.
Keep your tools sharp and your mug full. The rest sorts itself out.
Be kind to the cooks. They know where you sleep.
Don't argue with the overseer. Agree, then do it properly.
Enjoy it. This is a good fort, and good forts don't last forever.
Somebody fix things around here. That's all.
Things will get better. They have to.
Mind the stairs, thank the haulers, and never trust a carp.
Look up from your work now and then. This place is something.
Get some sleep. Whatever it is, it'll still be there in the morning.
Thank you for asking. Nobody ever asks.
Fix the beds. That's my final word.

child.text: When I grow up I'm going to be in charge.
Can I go now? I'm in the middle of a game.
Tell the cook I want honey.

baby.text: (The interview ended when the subject was collected for a nap.)
(The subject waved. We think it was a wave.)

q.text: You've just come back from {envoy_site}. How did it go?
What was it like, meeting {envoy_civ}?
Tell us about {envoy_met}.
Were you nervous, walking into {envoy_site} with the fort's letter?

contact.text: Long walk, short meeting. {envoy_met} heard me out, the {envoy_title} nodded, and now {envoy_civ} know where {fort} is. The proposal was {envoy_result}.
I said who we were and what we make. They'd never heard of us. They have now.
{envoy_met} wanted to know if we're the kind of dwarves who trade or the kind who raid. I said trade. I said it twice.

contact_lied.text: I may have made the fort sound a little bigger than it is. And richer. And closer. It worked, didn't it? {envoy_result}, they said.
Let's say I told {envoy_met} a story with some extra rooms in it. Diplomacy is mostly confidence.
Lying? I prefer ‘describing our future.’ {envoy_civ} will see it when the caravan arrives. Or they won't, and I'll be somewhere else.

good.text: It went well. {envoy_met} agreed, and I got a decent meal out of it.
Better than I hoped. The proposal was {envoy_result}.

bad.text: Not well. {envoy_met} listened politely and said no impolitely.
They weren't interested. I'll try again next year with a better hat.

nomeet.text: I walked all the way to {envoy_site} and there was nobody to talk to. Nobody in charge, anyway. I talked to a tree for a while.
Empty-handed. No one in {envoy_site} could speak for {envoy_civ}. The foreign office says try another town. My feet say no.
Long walk. Nice scenery. No meeting. I'm told that counts as diplomacy experience.

contact.text: “THEY'D NEVER HEARD OF US. THEY HAVE NOW”
“I SAID TRADE. I SAID IT TWICE”

contact_lied.text: THE ENVOY WHO LIED FOR THE FORT
“A STORY WITH SOME EXTRA ROOMS IN IT”

nomeet.text: “I TALKED TO A TREE FOR A WHILE”

q.text: You were at {raid_site}. What was it like?
How did the raid on {raid_site} go?
What did you bring back from {raid_site}?
Aren't we at peace with {raid_civ}?
I'm sorry about {raid_lost}. Do you want to talk about it?

war.text: Long march, short fight. They didn't expect us. We {raid_verb} {raid_site} and came home before the ale went flat.
Loud. Then quiet. Then we were carrying things. That's a raid.
Their walls were thinner than ours. Tell the masons that, they'll like it.
I brought back a story. The rest is in the stockpile.

peace.text: Officially, yes. Unofficially, we {raid_verb} {raid_site}. The war office says it's ‘antagonizing’. I say it's walking a long way to hit goblins.
Peace is what you call it until somebody notices. {raid_civ} have noticed.
They took one of our old forts. We took some of their things. Seems fair to me.

lost.text: Not really. {raid_lost} was next to me on the march out. Not on the march back.
We {raid_verb} {raid_site}. It cost us {raid_lost}. Ask me again next year if it was worth it.
I'll drink to {raid_lost} tonight. Then I'll sharpen my axe.

war.text: “LOUD. THEN QUIET. THEN WE WERE CARRYING THINGS”

peace.text: “PEACE IS WHAT YOU CALL IT UNTIL SOMEBODY NOTICES”

busy.text: We caught {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, while {doing}, and asked a few questions.
We found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, {doing}. They didn't stop, so neither did we.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, kept {doing} while we talked. Our reporter took notes and tried not to get in the way.
Our correspondent found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, busy {doing}, and borrowed a few minutes.

idle.text: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, had a free moment, which in {fort} is rare enough to make the paper.
We found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, with nothing to do, and gave them something: our questions.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was off duty and in a talking mood. We pulled up a chair.
Between shifts, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, sat down with our reporter for a few minutes.
Our correspondent found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, between jobs and asked about life in {fort}.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was taking a break when we called. They let us sit down.

sleep.text: We woke {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, for this interview. They have asked us not to do that again.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, answered our questions half asleep. We have tidied the answers a little.

break.text: We sat down with {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, over a meal and a mug.

mood.text: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, is in the grip of a strange mood and answered from behind a closed door.

child.text: {dwarf}, aged {age}, one of the youngest dwarves in {fort}, agreed to an interview in exchange for a sweet roll.

baby.text: {dwarf}, aged {age}, is the youngest dwarf we have ever interviewed. Questions were answered on the subject's behalf by the subject.
